Front: What is the core architectural decision in AI-assisted paper research?
Back: Human-in-the-loop triage (higher quality, slower) vs fully autonomous pipeline (faster, quality ceiling lower). Choose human-in-the-loop for strategic decisions and novel domains; fully autonomous for monitoring known fields and weekly digests.

Front: What are the five stages of a production-grade AI research pipeline?
Back: Discover (Elicit/Semantic Scholar/ArXiv) -> Triage (score papers) -> Extract (structured JSON) -> Critique (find weaknesses) -> Synthesize (cross-paper themes and contradictions). Human gates placed after triage and after synthesis.

Front: What four dimensions are used to score papers during triage?
Back: Novelty (1-5), Technical Depth (1-5), Relevance (1-5), Reproducibility (1-5). Threshold: total >= 12/20 to proceed to deep reading. 20% false-negative rate is acceptable since citation graphs catch missed papers.

Front: What is the key difference between NotebookLM's cross-document reasoning and RAG?
Back: NotebookLM reasons over full text of uploaded documents in a single context window, enabling cross-document comparison ("what do A and B disagree on?"). RAG retrieves chunks independently and loses cross-document coherence needed for contradiction detection.

Front: What is the recommended structured extraction schema for research papers?
Back: A 12-field JSON record: title, authors, problem, method, dataset, metrics, results, limitations, applicability, reproducibility_score, claims[] (text + evidence + confidence), and relationships[] (paper + type: extends/contradicts/uses).

Front: How should you detect and prevent citation hallucination in agentic pipelines?
Back: Never trust LLM-generated references. Verify every citation against Semantic Scholar API (/paper/search endpoint) before storage. Check title similarity >0.9 against results. Flag any reference that returns no match. S2 free tier: 100 requests per 5 minutes.

Front: What is the cost model for a weekly agentic literature review (20 papers discovered, 5 deep-read)?
Back: Total approximately $7.25/week: Discovery $0 (Elicit free), Triage $0.20 (Haiku, 20 papers), Deep extraction $2.50 (Sonnet, 5 papers), Critique $1.50, Embedding $0.05, Synthesis $3.00 (Sonnet 200K context).

Front: What is the primary cost optimization strategy for AI research pipelines?
Back: Model routing: use Haiku for triage (80% of volume at $0.01/paper) and Sonnet only for papers that pass threshold (deep extraction at $0.50/paper). This achieves 40-50% cost reduction without quality loss on the high-value stages.

Front: Why should you embed structured extractions rather than full paper text?
Back: Full-text embeddings dilute signal with boilerplate (related work, acknowledgments). Structured embeddings (problem + method + results) are denser and more query-relevant. Typical retrieval precision@10: structured ~0.72 vs full-text ~0.45.

Front: What are the three levels of hierarchical embedding for research papers?
Back: Level 0: Paper-level (title + abstract) for broad discovery. Level 1: Section-level (each major section) for methodology search. Level 2: Claim-level (each extracted claim) for fact verification. Storage cost increases 15x but enables queries at different specificity.

Front: How does the Bayesian triage calibration loop work?
Back: Track human reading decisions (override = reads a rejected paper, or skips an accepted one). Update dimension weights: false negatives increase weight of highest-scoring dimension; false positives decrease it. Normalize weights to sum=1. Converges after ~50 examples.

Front: What is the "cold start" strategy for building a research knowledge base?
Back: 1) Find 1-2 recent survey papers. 2) Extract reference list as seed corpus. 3) Use Semantic Scholar API for citation graph. 4) Deep-read top 10 most-cited. 5) Use Connected Papers for visual exploration. 6) Expand from clusters, not keyword search.

Front: How do Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini compare for paper analysis tasks?
Back: Claude: best for methodological critique and adversarial reasoning. ChatGPT: best for structured extraction (JSON mode with schema compliance). Gemini 2.5 Pro: best for very long papers (80+ pages) with 1M+ native context. For triage/summary: use cheapest.

Front: What is the hardest-to-detect failure mode in automated literature reviews?
Back: Plausible but wrong synthesis - when the review connects findings in a way that sounds correct but misrepresents causal relationships. Example: "A shows X improves Y; B shows Y improves Z; therefore X improves Z" - transitivity doesn't necessarily hold but reads convincingly.

Front: What is the cross-paper contradiction detection approach?
Back: Extract claims as structured triples (subject, predicate, object, condition, magnitude, dataset). Compare pairwise: same subject+object but different predicate with condition similarity >0.8 flags potential contradiction. LLM-as-judge evaluates if real, reducing false positives by ~70%.

Front: What percentage of a research workflow can realistically be automated?
Back: ~80% of volume (discovery, triage, extraction, storage) but only ~20% of value (insights come from synthesis and critique requiring human judgment). The automation handles "reading 30 papers to find 5 worth your time."

Front: What are the four requirements for converting a manual research workflow into an executable agentic SOP?
Back: 1) Every input is machine-readable (PDF to text, query to API call). 2) Every decision has a numeric threshold (not "use judgment"). 3) Every output is structured (JSON, not prose). 4) Every escalation point is defined (when to involve human).

Front: What is Semantic Scholar's role in agentic research pipelines?
Back: Open academic graph with 200M+ papers. Powers both discovery (recommendation feeds, citation graph traversal) and verification (citation existence checks). Key endpoints: /paper/search, /paper/{id}/references, /paper/{id}/citations, /recommendations. Free API: 100 req/5min.

Front: When does a vector database add value vs a JSON file with grep for research papers?
Back: At 50 papers, a JSON file with grep is faster to build, easier to debug, and sufficient. Vector DB adds value at 200+ papers when keyword search stops working for semantic queries.

Front: What three architectural patterns can orchestrate research agent pipelines?
Back: State Machine (LangGraph): easy to reason about, sequential, best for single-paper deep analysis. DAG (Airflow/Prefect): parallel processing, fixed topology, best for batch 20+ papers. Event-Driven (Temporal): dynamic workflows, long-running, best for continuous monitoring.

Front: What is the recommended hybrid architecture for research pipeline orchestration?
Back: DAG (outer loop): weekly batch of 20 papers, parallel triage. State Machine (inner loop): per-paper analysis with decisions. Event-Driven (trigger): new paper alert injected into next batch.

Front: What five dimensions should be used to evaluate automated literature review quality?
Back: Coverage (key papers found), Accuracy (factual correctness), Synthesis (logical connections between papers), Actionability (specific takeaways), Citation Quality (real and correctly attributed references).

Front: Why is a "skeptic" judge essential in multi-judge evaluation of literature reviews?
Back: The skeptic is specifically prompted to find hallucinated claims, unsupported connections, and missing caveats. Without it, reviews score artificially high because LLM judges default to charitable interpretation.

Front: What is the knowledge base decay model and what are typical half-lives by field?
Back: current_relevance = initial_relevance * 0.5^(age_months/half_life). Half-lives: ML/AI = 18 months, Systems = 36 months, Theory = 60 months. Archive papers when relevance drops below 0.3.

Front: How should paper deduplication work across venues (arXiv preprint, conference, journal)?
Back: Detect via: title similarity >0.95, OR author overlap >80% AND abstract similarity >0.85. Keep most recent/authoritative version, link others as "superseded_by."

Front: What is the cascade problem in research knowledge base maintenance?
Back: When a foundational paper's claims change (e.g., arXiv v1 to v2), every synthesis that references it may be invalid. Track dependency graphs (synthesis.depends_on = [paper_A, paper_B]) and trigger re-evaluation when any dependency updates.

Front: What is the minimal viable AI research pipeline that delivers value in one week?
Back: Claude API + single Python script: download PDF, extract with structured prompt, append JSON to a file, weekly manual review. No vector DB, no embeddings, no state machine. Add infrastructure only when the JSON file exceeds ~100 papers.

Front: What is the key bottleneck in research that AI tools solve?
Back: The bottleneck in research is not finding papers - it's deciding which ones deserve 2 hours of your time. AI tools solve discovery; an agentic pipeline solves triage; but human judgment still owns the 'so what?'

Front: What distinguishes domain-specific pipeline calibration from generic research automation?
Back: Domain-specific calibration is the whole point. A pipeline tuned for ML papers (fast decay, code emphasis) fails for clinical trials (slow decay, methodology emphasis). Generality is the enemy of precision in research pipelines.

Front: How does the feedback loop work in a production research agent?
Back: Published reports reveal coverage gaps ("we have no papers on X") which generate new discovery keywords fed back to the discovery stage. This makes the system self-improving in coverage without requiring self-improving models.

Front: When does embedding-based search fail for research papers?
Back: When the query is about methodology specifics (e.g., "papers using contrastive loss with negative sampling >100"). Embeddings capture semantic similarity but miss precise technical constraints. Solution: extract methodology keywords into structured fields and combine with exact-match filters.

Front: What is the optimal placement of human gates in an AI research pipeline?
Back: Exactly two points: (1) Post-triage (confirm which papers deserve deep reads) and (2) Post-synthesis (confirm narrative before it enters knowledge base). Every stage without review compounds error; every approval adds latency.

Front: What storage strategy tiers should a research knowledge base use?
Back: Hot (active search, <6 months old), Warm (searchable but lower ranking, 6-24 months), Cold (archived, only direct lookup, >24 months or relevance <0.3).

Front: How do you replicate NotebookLM's cross-document reasoning in a custom pipeline?
Back: Use Claude's 1M-token context: concatenate full texts of top-K most relevant papers (by embedding similarity to query), then prompt for cross-paper synthesis. Cost: ~$0.50 per synthesis query at 200K tokens. Works for up to ~15-20 full papers per query.

Front: What is the hybrid search approach for a research knowledge base?
Back: Combine embedding similarity (semantic, 70% weight) with BM25 keyword ranking (exact match, 30% weight). SQL: (embedding <=> query_embedding) * 0.7 + ts_rank(to_tsvector(extraction), query) * 0.3.
